title: Amazon Blocks Meta’s Muse From Shopping on Its Marketplace
summary: Amazon has cut off Meta’s Muse agent, escalating a conflict over whether AI assistants may browse and transact without merchant approval.
body:
## Amazon draws a line

Amazon has blocked Meta’s Muse personal AI agent from shopping on Amazon.com, saying Meta did not obtain permission for the service to access its marketplace. Amazon said Muse did not identify itself as an automated agent and appeared to capture or store customer credentials, creating privacy and security concerns.

Users attempting to shop through Muse saw a warning that continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violated Amazon’s Conditions of Use. Meta has previously said that Muse stores credentials securely and cannot see users’ passwords or payment details.

## A dispute over the transaction layer

The conflict is bigger than one blocked assistant. Muse was designed to browse services through a virtual browser when no public API is available, allowing it to compare products, fill carts and complete purchases after user approval. Amazon argues that third-party agents should operate openly and respect a merchant’s decision about whether to participate.

The dispute also exposes competing business incentives. Amazon is building its own shopping agents, including tools that identify themselves and give merchants an opt-out path, while its advertising business depends heavily on controlling the browsing experience and sponsored product exposure.

Amazon’s action follows a broader effort to restrict outside agents, including previous disputes involving Perplexity and other AI companies. A recent US appellate ruling weakened one possible anti-hacking route for Amazon but left contract and terms-of-service arguments available.

## Uncle Cat take

The decisive fact is that Muse’s headline shopping capability can disappear when a single marketplace withdraws access. That makes platform permission, rather than model competence, the immediate bottleneck for agentic commerce. Meta may have a strong consumer distribution advantage, but until agents become identifiable, auditable and commercially welcome to merchants, their promised autonomy remains conditional.
title_zh: 亚马逊封锁Meta Muse，AI代理购物遭遇平台边界
summary_zh: 亚马逊切断Meta Muse的购物访问，代理能否未经商家授权浏览并下单，正成为智能体商业化的关键冲突。
body_zh:
## 亚马逊划出红线

亚马逊已阻止Meta的个人AI智能体Muse在Amazon.com上购物，理由是Meta没有获得平台授权。亚马逊称，Muse没有明确表明自己是自动化智能体，并疑似捕获或保存用户凭证，由此带来隐私与安全风险。

用户通过Muse购物时会看到提示，称未经授权的AI智能体继续访问违反亚马逊使用条款。Meta此前则表示，Muse会安全保存凭证，无法看到用户密码或支付信息。

## 争夺交易入口

这场冲突并不只是一个助手被封锁。Muse的设计是：当服务没有公开API时，通过虚拟浏览器像用户一样访问网站，从而完成比价、加入购物车，并在用户确认后下单。亚马逊认为，第三方智能体应公开自己的自动化身份，也应尊重商家是否愿意参与。

争议背后还有商业利益冲突。亚马逊正在开发自己的购物智能体，包括能够主动表明身份、并为商家提供退出机制的工具；与此同时，其广告业务高度依赖对用户浏览过程和赞助商品曝光的控制。

这次封锁也是亚马逊限制外部智能体行动的一部分，此前Perplexity等公司也曾与其发生争议。美国近期一项上诉法院裁决削弱了亚马逊依据反黑客法律维权的路径，但合同和使用条款仍可能成为平台限制智能体的依据。

## 猫叔判断

最关键的事实是：Muse最醒目的购物能力，可以因一个大型市场撤回访问而立刻失效。对代理式电商而言，眼下真正的瓶颈不是模型会不会下单，而是平台是否允许它进入交易现场。Meta拥有强大的消费者分发能力，但在智能体做到可识别、可审计并获得商家认可之前，它的自主性始终是有条件的。
